  "summary": "General Secretary Girish Munshi’s Circular No. 322, dated 1 May 1975, reports to Swatantra Party members on the party’s response to Jayaprakash Narayan’s effort to unite the non-Congress and non-Communist opposition. It recounts concerns about the growing ineffectiveness of parliamentary processes, the concentration of power in the Prime Minister’s hands, corruption, and the failure of the Bharatiya Lok Dal (BLD) to become a genuinely national alternative. Rather than an immediate merger, the circular supports a federal structure in which parties retain their identities while working on a common programme, election strategy, symbol, and candidate-selection process.\n\nThe circular strongly endorses Narayan’s movement and his ideas of Sarvodaya, peaceful “Total Revolution,” popular resistance to oppressive state power, and preservation of fundamental rights. It also records Swatantra Party decisions and organisational developments between January and April 1975, including support for electoral reforms, demands for more accurate electoral rolls, opposition to industrial controls and quotas, legal challenges over the party’s election symbol, and efforts to revive state units in Uttar Pradesh, Orissa, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Maharashtra. The document ends by presenting the party as recovering from earlier difficulties and anticipating slow but steady growth.",

      "It endorses Jayaprakash Narayan’s leadership and associates his movement with Sarvodaya, non-violent Total Revolution, popular power, and fundamental rights.",
      "It calls for a common opposition election strategy, common election symbol, minimum programme, and honest candidates regardless of party affiliation.",
      "It records the Swatantra Party’s support for electoral reform, accurate voter rolls, and adequate notice for objections.",
      "It criticises industrial controls and quota systems, attributing under-capacity partly to shortages of raw materials and controls over prices and distribution.",
      "It reports party reorganisation, court proceedings over the election symbol, and attempts to rebuild state-level units."
